public_rationale: Read plainly, he says AI could not, as of August 2025, take over software development so that coding could just be handed to it. METR's independent evaluation of GPT-5, published August 7, 2025, found the model succeeded about half the time on software tasks that take a professional about 2 hours 17 minutes. It reached 80% success only on tasks of about 25 minutes, similar to other frontier models. A system that fails that often on short, well-defined tasks cannot be relied on to handle coding on its own, especially for users who cannot check its work. I found no credible evidence from that time of AI reliably building complete working software without human coding expertise. The plain reading is supported.
limitations: The claim has no stated threshold, so the result depends on the plain reading of 'just handle coding.'
The evidence is one evaluator's benchmark. Real projects differ from its tasks.
AI coding ability rose quickly after the post. This assessment covers only the state around August 2025.

He describes the current state without naming a period. I use the period just before the post (July 1 to August 25, 2025), when the latest frontier models had been released and independently measured.
Independent measurements of how reliably frontier AI agents complete realistic software-engineering tasks on their own are fair evidence.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence from around the post date shows AI systems reliably completing realistic software development work end to end, without human coding expertise, at a level where coding could be handed off to them.

evidence.explanation: The leading frontier model at the post date failed about half the time on software tasks a professional finishes in roughly two hours. That fits the claim that AI could not simply be handed coding work.
